newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGRI-LA PAYS HK$1.2 BLN IN SHRS FOR SLIM INT'L.
newsitem.headline: SHANGRI-LA PAYS HK$1.2 BLN IN SHRS FOR SLIM INT'L.

text.p: Shangri-La Asia Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy 100 percent of hotel management and marketing company SLIM International Ltd from the Kuok Group for HK$1.2 billion in shares.
Shangri-La Asia said it would issue 135.9 million new shares to the Kuok Group, Shangri-La Asia's parent, at HK$8.83 per share.
SLIM International is the holding company of the hotel management and marketing subsidiaries of the Shangri-La group, known as Shangri-La Hotels and Resorts, Shangri-La Asia said in a statement.
It manages hotels and resorts principally owned by Shangri-La Asia and other members of the Kuok Group as well as third party owners.
SLIM International had proforma net profit before tax of HK$91.8 million in 1996 compared with HK$73.6 million in 1995.
Proforma net asset value of the group at the end of 1996 was HK$123.8 million.
Through SLIM International, Shangri-La Asia said it would have 35 hotels under management after the transaction.
It said two Shangri-La hotels would be opened in 1997 and three more were scheduled to be opened in 1998.
"We view this acquisition as a natural step in the process of growing our business and broadening our reach," Shangri-La Asia chairman Liu Tai Fung said in the statement.
"SLIM's operations will complement the existing business of Shangri-La Asia and provide another steady source of recurring income which we believe has very good growth potential."
